correctness.rationale: The eligible-face incidence probability of a vertex of degree k is exactly (k+1)/(n+E_n), giving all conditional degree-count drifts without an independence assumption for the two endpoints of a chosen edge. Edge density x=E_n/n solves stable stochastic approximation to golden ratio phi. The stated bounded martingale-increment stability lemma applies to each fixed degree class by induction; the countable intersection yields simultaneous almost-sure limits. Summing the fixed-point balances gives (1+phi) sum_(k<=K) p_k =1+phi-(K+1)p_K, and the gamma ratio gives K p_K->0, hence normalized distribution and total variation. Correct boundary degree classes and no claim for k=k(n). Independently recomputed p1,p2 and partial mass through 100000 (~0.999999999998).
